about: Stockway Pro v1 (3.01, Mandeep 24 Nov 2026: option buying only; every input votes together, no separate Ghanshyam / pattern boxes; strong checks; after the close, which check really lined up and worked). The numbers live here (bullets); live/pro.py is the gun. On trial: two paper accounts (Pro · Index, Pro · Stocks) and the Pro page; nothing else you see, Telegram, Focus or the main account changes.
weights_why: forecast 0: the next-candle direction was right 50-51% of the time (the plain 'keeps its colour' rule as good). mindgame 0: its all-bullet lean is replaced by pro_mind (only the bullets that beat a coin flip in the 5-year check, and taken_back turned round). daytype: the 09:45 day-type forecaster (trend days: the 09:45 move pointed the day's way 78-83%).

mind.why: 5-year Bank Nifty check: gap_booking 56% / 57%, trap_run 53% (5m), range_trap 58% (15m); taken_back right only 40% / 37%, so its opposite (60-63%) votes.

expiry_why: 23 Nov (monthly expiry): the same-day-expiry buys after 11:00 lost 7 of 8 (net -Rs3,013 against what was kept). 3.04 (Mandeep, 24 Nov: 'koi aisa lock nahi chahiye ki aache alert aaye toh system trade hi na le; market situation dekhni hai but opportunity miss nahi karni'): no longer a time lock. After 11:00 on a same-day expiry a strong signal is still bought, unless the move-vs-decay check votes against it (the expected move does not beat the time decay).
cooloff_why: Off from 3.04 (Mandeep: no lock on good signals). Was 15: on 23 Nov a second buy on the same index and side 3 minutes after the first one's exit (FINNIFTY 09:35, NIFTY 09:35) never went green: -Rs36K. One day only; the re-buys are now taken and graded on new days.
exit_why: 23 Nov: Bank Nifty PE went +79% and closed -40% (trailing account -Rs13,790); locking +25% once it is +50% would have kept ~+Rs8,300.
learn_why: Weights learn from new days only: a factor's weight moves only with 100+ graded signals, by 25% at most, and the new weights must beat the old ones on the next 5 market days they never saw before they are used.
